mcqs.q: A gland is best defined as:
opts: A secretory organ of specialized epithelial cells derived from surface epithelium
mcqs.explain: A gland is an organ of secretion made of specialized secretory cells derived from the surface epithelium on which it opens; glands are epithelial in origin.

mcqs.q: The flask-shaped secretory end piece of a gland is called a(n):
mcqs.explain: Secretory end pieces are flask-shaped (acinus) or cylindrical (tubular); they are the functional secretory units.

mcqs.q: Myoepithelial cells are:
opts: Star-shaped contractile cells that expel secretion from the acini
mcqs.explain: Myoepithelial cells are star-shaped, contractile cells lying between the secretory cells and the basement membrane; they contract to expel the secretory product.

mcqs.q: Myoepithelial cells lie between the secretory cells and the:
mcqs.explain: Myoepithelial cells sit between the secretory cells and the basement membrane, hugging the acinus.

mcqs.q: Serous acini produce a secretion that is:
mcqs.explain: Serous acini secrete a thin, watery, enzyme-rich fluid; mucous acini secrete a thick, viscous mucus.

mcqs.q: The nucleus of a SEROUS cell is typically:
mcqs.explain: Serous cells have a round, central nucleus, whereas mucous cells have a flat nucleus pushed to the periphery (base).

mcqs.q: Mucous acini are characterised by a nucleus that is:
opts: Flat and pushed to the periphery (base)
mcqs.explain: In mucous cells the accumulated mucigen flattens the nucleus and pushes it to the basal periphery; the lumen is large.

mcqs.q: On H&E staining, serous acini appear:
mcqs.explain: Serous acini stain deeply with H&E (zymogen granules), while mucous acini stain lightly/palely.

mcqs.q: The secretory granules of serous cells are called:
mcqs.explain: Serous cells contain zymogen granules (enzyme precursors); mucous cells contain mucigen droplets.

mcqs.q: Which gland is the classic example of a purely SEROUS gland?
mcqs.explain: The parotid is a purely serous gland; the sublingual is predominantly mucous.

mcqs.q: During development, a gland forms by:
opts: Invagination of surface epithelium into the underlying connective tissue
mcqs.explain: A gland develops as an invagination (downgrowth) of epithelium into the underlying vascular connective tissue.

mcqs.q: In gland development, the DISTAL part of the epithelial downgrowth forms the:
mcqs.explain: The distal part becomes the secretory (glandular) end piece, while the proximal part forms the excretory duct that opens on the surface.

mcqs.q: Striated ducts are recognised histologically by:
opts: Basal striations (infolded membranes packed with mitochondria)
mcqs.explain: Striated ducts modify saliva (reabsorb Na⁺, secrete K⁺); their basal striations are infolded cell membranes packed with mitochondria.

mcqs.q: The histology of the PAROTID gland shows:
opts: Serous acini, many ducts and adipocyte (fat) infiltration
mcqs.explain: The parotid contains serous acini, a large number of ducts, and characteristic adipocyte (fat) infiltration.

mcqs.q: The submandibular gland is described histologically as:
opts: A mixed gland (mostly serous + few mucous) with serous demilunes
mcqs.explain: The submandibular is a mixed gland — many serous and few mucous acini, many striated ducts, and serous demilunes.

mcqs.q: A 'serous demilune' is:
opts: A crescent-shaped cap of serous cells on a mucous acinus
mcqs.explain: Serous demilunes are crescent (half-moon) caps of serous cells sitting on the periphery of mucous acini in mixed glands.

mcqs.q: The sublingual gland is predominantly:
mcqs.explain: The sublingual gland contains mainly mucous acini and few striated ducts.

mcqs.q: Compared with serous acini, mucous acini have a lumen that is:
mcqs.explain: Mucous acini have a large lumen, whereas serous acini have a small lumen.

mcqs.q: Secretion from the acini is modulated by:
mcqs.explain: Glandular secretion is modulated by both nervous and hormonal influences.

mcqs.q: Which secretory product is NOT typically produced by glands in general?
mcqs.explain: Glandular secretions are enzymes, hormones or mucus; bone matrix is produced by osteoblasts, not glands.

saqs.q: Define a gland and describe its secretory end pieces and myoepithelial cells.
saqs.a: An epithelial secretory organ from surface epithelium. End pieces are acini (flask) or tubules (cylinder). Myoepithelial cells — star-shaped, contractile, between secretory cells and basement membrane — squeeze the acini to expel secretion.

saqs.q: Compare serous and mucous acini (secretion, nucleus, lumen, stain, example).
saqs.a: Serous: thin watery, round central nucleus, small lumen, deeply stained, zymogen (parotid). Mucous: thick viscous, flat peripheral nucleus, large lumen, lightly stained, mucigen (sublingual).
By invagination of epithelium into vascular connective tissue: the distal part forms the secretory end piece and the proximal part forms the excretory duct opening on the surface.

saqs.q: What are striated ducts and what do they do?
saqs.a: Intralobular ducts with basal striations (infolded membranes packed with mitochondria) that modify saliva — reabsorbing Na⁺ and secreting K⁺.

saqs.q: Describe the histology of the three major glands.
saqs.a: Parotid: serous acini + many ducts + fat. Submandibular: mixed (mostly serous, few mucous) + striated ducts + serous demilunes. Sublingual: mainly mucous + few striated ducts.

saqs.q: What is a serous demilune and where is it found?
saqs.a: A crescent-shaped cap of serous cells on the periphery of a mucous acinus, found in mixed glands such as the submandibular.

saqs.q: List the general histological components of a salivary gland.
saqs.a: Acini (serous/mucous secretory units), ducts (incl. striated), a basement membrane, and myoepithelial cells; supported by connective tissue (and fat in the parotid).
